blocks.prompt: 8 The position vectors of the points \(A, B, C\) and \(D\) are \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 7\underline{i} + 8\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -\underline{i} + \underline{k}\) and \(\underline{z} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) respectively. Show that \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) is parallel to \(\overrightarrow{CD}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof: two vectors are parallel when one is a scalar multiple of the other.
We must find \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CD}\) from the position vectors.
Plan: \(\overrightarrow{AB} = \underline{v} - \underline{u}\), \(\overrightarrow{CD} = \underline{z} - \underline{w}\), then find \(c\) with \(\overrightarrow{AB} = c\,\overrightarrow{CD}\).
steps:
Given: position vectors \(\underline{u}\) (of \(A\)), \(\underline{v}\) (of \(B\)), \(\underline{w}\) (of \(C\)), \(\underline{z}\) (of \(D\)).
To prove: \(\overrightarrow{AB} \parallel \overrightarrow{CD}\).
Method: \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = \) (position vector of \(Q\)) \(-\) (position vector of \(P\)); vectors are parallel when one is a scalar multiple of the other.

Find \(\overrightarrow{AB}\)
\[\overrightarrow{AB} = \underline{v} - \underline{u}\]
\[= (7 - 1)\underline{i} + (8 - 2)\underline{j} + (4 - 1)\underline{k}\]
\[= 6\underline{i} + 6\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
Why: End point \(B\) minus start point \(A\).

Find \(\overrightarrow{CD}\)
\[\overrightarrow{CD} = \underline{z} - \underline{w}\]
\[= (1 - (-1))\underline{i} + (2 - 0)\underline{j} + (2 - 1)\underline{k}\]
\[= 2\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\]
Why: End point \(D\) minus start point \(C\); \(\underline{w}\) has no \(\underline{j}\) term, so its \(\underline{j}\) component is 0.

Compare the two vectors
\[\overrightarrow{AB} = 6\underline{i} + 6\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
\[= 3(2\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \underline{k})\]
\[= 3\,\overrightarrow{CD}\]
Why: 3 is a common factor of 6, 6 and 3, and what remains is exactly \(\overrightarrow{CD}\). So \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) is a scalar multiple (\(c = 3 > 0\)) of \(\overrightarrow{CD}\).

Check (lengths)
\[|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{36 + 36 + 9} = 9\]
\[|\overrightarrow{CD}| = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3\]
Why: The lengths are in the ratio \(9 : 3 = 3\), matching \(c = 3\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\overrightarrow{AB} = 3\,\overrightarrow{CD}\), so \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) is parallel to \(\overrightarrow{CD}\).
